title: Launch and Harden an EC2 Instance
description: Draft a user data script and security group setup for a public web server.
problemStatement:
Write a user data script (bash) that:
- Updates all installed packages.
- Installs the Apache web server (httpd).
- Starts the service and enables it on boot.
- Creates a simple index.html that displays the instance ID (retrieved from metadata) and the current date.

Then describe the security group rules you would apply to this web server for maximum security while still serving public web traffic. Assume you will manage the server via SSH from your home IP (203.0.113.25).
hints: The instance metadata service is at http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/.
For security, SSH must be restricted to your IP. HTTP/HTTPS can be public.
Consider restricting outbound traffic as well (though not strictly necessary).
expectedOutput: A bash script and a description of security group rules.
solutionCode:
User data script: ```bash #!/bin/bash yum update -y yum install -y httpd systemctl start httpd systemctl enable httpd INSTANCE_ID=$(curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id) echo "

Instance ID: $INSTANCE_ID

Deployed on: $(date)

" > /var/www/html/index.html ``` Security group rules: - Inbound: HTTP (80) source 0.0.0.0/0 - Inbound: HTTPS (443) source 0.0.0.0/0 (if you later configure SSL) - Inbound: SSH (22) source 203.0.113.25/32 - Outbound: all traffic allowed (default) – or restrict to specific services (e.g., 80/443 for updates) if extremely paranoid.
